images.name: Gridline — typography-led home
images.role: Future Kestrel material, form and lighting reference; home layout remains exploratory
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high fidelity full-screen desktop main-menu design for the anti-gravity racing game VECTOR//NOVA. This is an image of the game UI itself, edge to edge, landscape 16:9, no device frame, no browser chrome, no moodboard, no swatch palette. Crisp legible restrained typography and convincing real game environment / vehicle rendering. Purpose: explore a distinct professional game-menu layout.
COLOR IS CRITICAL: strictly neutral blacks and greys (#090909, #171717, #262626) with neutral white #E8E8E8. The ONLY UI accent is straight deep RED #A81010, with small brighter pure-red #D01818 selected marks if needed, red darkens toward #300606. Red hue must have equal green and blue channels, hue exactly red: NO orange, rust, terracotta, salmon, coral, vermilion, pink, magenta, burgundy, maroon or wine. NO warm/cream whites, NO blue-grey surfaces. Keep 90-95% of the UI neutral black/grey; red is a small, precise signal, never a broad red-tinted gradient. Lighting neutral, not sunset orange. Avoid generic AI website styling: no glowing gradient blobs, no glassmorphism, no pill navigation, no rounded dashboard cards, no decorative grids, no gratuitous sci-fi data gibberish, no meaningless HUD glyphs. Typography uses disciplined large sans-serif racing/editorial lettering with useful small labels. Strong asymmetry, deliberate negative space. Render text exactly as supplied. No extra slogans.
Game context: a fast low-slung anti-gravity craft, slender split nose, swept ceramic chassis, graphite and machined titanium, no wheels. The ship is an original angular race craft, not a fighter jet or car. Only small true-red painted identifiers on a neutral ceramic hull.
LAYOUT A — GRIDLINE. A severely clean motorsport title menu. Left 39% is a perfectly flat near-black editorial column with "VECTOR//NOVA" at the top, ample blank space, then a large vertically stacked main menu. Exact entries: "QUICK RACE", "PRACTICE", "FLEET", "SETTINGS". QUICK RACE selected: white type with one narrow pure-red rectangular marker at left and a subtle red underline, not a big colored button. A small line underneath reads "2 LAPS / 4 SHIPS". Bottom left contains a very small "ENTER  SELECT".
Right 61% is a sharp, cinematic close crop of the ceramic/graphite anti-gravity craft at an elevated city starting grid at NIGHT, almost monochrome, softly lit by white pit lighting. Close crop emphasizes machined surfaces, front split nose and swept planform. Architecture recedes into darkness, no red/orange sky, no cyan glow. Image crops confidently at right edge. A small restrained label near bottom right reads "HALCYON SPEEDWAY" with "KESTREL / BALANCED" beneath. One very thin vertical red rule cleanly separates the left column from the cinematic crop. The total screen should feel purposeful, spare and physically grounded, like a real racing game front end rather than a tech startup homepage.

LAYOUT C — CIRCUIT WALL. A complete circuit-selection screen, clearly a game UI. Compact top bar: left "VECTOR//NOVA", then "QUICK RACE", right "BACK". Below it at top left the large heading "SELECT CIRCUIT".
Left 62% holds six landscape track cards in a precise 2-column by 3-row grid with generous black gutters. Square corners, no shadows. Each card has an understated darkened environment still and a clear thin neutral-white route-outline diagram overlaid on it. The route diagrams are distinct racing circuits, small enough not to obliterate the environment. Cards are labeled exactly "HALCYON SPEEDWAY", "ASTERION ORBITAL", "NACRE TEMPEST", "VESPER CANOPY", "CINDERCOIL", "UMBRA FOLD". Atmospheric thumbnails: city viaduct, orbital shipyard, storm ocean, enormous tree canopy, volcanic infrastructure, accretion observatory; keep thumbnails mostly monochrome for this palette study, not saturated sci-fi artwork. Halcyon selected with one 2px pure-red frame and a small pure-red index marker, all other frames neutral.
Right 38% is one open editorial detail area without a boxed card: a large cinematic city-raceway image upper right, generous black underneath, large text "HALCYON" then smaller "SPEEDWAY", one short line "5.00 KM / 2 LAPS / 3 RIVALS". At bottom right a substantial sharp rectangular true-deep-red button labeled "CHOOSE SHIP" in neutral white with a small simple arrow. Footer across screen minimal "SELECT CIRCUIT" and "CONTINUE". Hierarchy must let player compare all six circuits immediately and understand the selected track. Keep route-line art elegant and useful; no noisy dashboards, no extra stats, no badges. This is a screenshot of a coherent game screen, not a collage of unrelated designs.
